paragraphs: Ranpak Holdings Corp. ("Ranpak," the "Company," "we," or "us") is a leading provider of Protective Packaging Solutions ("PPS") products and end-of-line automation solutions for e-commerce and industrial supply chains. Since our inception in 1972, we have delivered a broad array of value-added solutions to global customers, while maintaining our commitment to environmental sustainability. All of our packaging solutions are 100% recyclable, renewable, and biodegradable. Our automation solutions reduce packing time and materials, resulting in significant cost savings for our customers. We continue to work to respond to customer needs and develop innovative products and a comprehensive suite of solutions that improve supply chain performance, reduce costs and environmental impact, and deliver value.

In 2025, we generated net revenue of $395.0 million. Our revenues are geographically diverse, with approximately 47% of our 2025 net revenue generated in North America, approximately 45% generated in Europe, and approximately 8% generated in Asia and other locations. We have over 145,000 installed systems serving over 30,000 end-users as of December 31, 2025. We historically have benefited from net revenue that is recurring in nature with attractive profit margins from our installed base, resulting in strong payback periods and returns on invested capital per PPS system.
We believe that our business benefits from multiple factors that will drive our future growth:

•Growth of E-commerce. E-commerce is a significant growth driver in our business. Approximately 40% of our net revenue is derived from sales to e-commerce end-users. We continue to believe that global investment in e-commerce provides a significant opportunity for us as e-commerce continues to grow and outpaces growth in retail sales.

•Demand for Automation and Machine Vision. Our Automation and Machine Vision product lines provide many high-volume businesses with significant improvements to end-of-line packaging speed, reduced labor, material and shipping costs, and the generation of valuable data and statistics on end-of-line performance. As businesses continue to focus on efficiency and automated solutions, we believe many will look for ways to improve production efficiencies and quality, driving further demand for our automated and machine vision product lines.

•Expansion into Cold Chain. Sales to end-users in the food and beverage industry represented approximately 3% of our net revenue in 2025, but we believe businesses and consumers are increasingly demonstrating preferences for environmentally sustainable cold chain solutions to keep food and beverages cold during transit. We have expanded our offering to include fiber-based liners and sustainable plant-based cool packs to keep perishable goods cool while they are being delivered to consumers, such as the RecyCold® climaliner Plus™. Innovative solutions such as the RecyCold Climaliner plus represent a 100% paper-based recyclable liner replacement for expanded polystyrene foam or other less sustainable cold chain options, while still ensuring that products stay within their ideal temperature range for up to 72 hours.

•Focus on Sustainability. We believe that preference for environmentally sustainable packaging solutions will be a key driver of growth moving forward, particularly to the extent plastics and other resin-based solutions come under increasing public scrutiny and regulatory pressure, and we believe consumers are continuing to demonstrate an increasing preference for environmentally sustainable solutions. For example, we believe there is a substantial opportunity to expand our consumable offering through environmentally friendly alternatives to traditional plastic mailers, such as naturemailer™, a fully curbside recyclable mailer that utilizes honeycomb paper insulation.

•Continued Product Development and Innovation. We believe our ability to consistently innovate and add products to our portfolio through internal development and mergers and acquisitions ("M&A") will provide us with additional growth opportunities.

•Geographic Expansion. Historically, geographic expansion has fueled our growth, and we believe further geographic expansion and penetration of existing markets will continue to drive our future growth. Our full-service paper conversion facility in Malaysia became operational in the second half of 2024, and we believe the Malaysia facility has continued to improve our ability to serve customers in the region by shortening lead times as well and providing a more attractive cost profile to the Asia Pacific ("APAC") market than we have historically
been able to offer. Combined with the localized presence and connection to Southeast Asia, we believe the Malaysia facility can continue to bring favorable growth opportunities.

We seek to enhance our position as a leading global provider of innovative sustainable packaging and end-of-line automation and machine vision solutions. To achieve these goals, we are focused on the following strategic priorities:

•Automation and Machine Vision. Our Automation products represented 10% of our net revenue in 2025, compared to 8% of our net revenue in 2024. We believe Automation will be a crucial platform for growth, enabling us to better serve end-users with higher volume requirements and more sophisticated end-of-line needs. In 2021, we established R Squared Robotics, a division of Ranpak, that uses three-dimensional computer vision and artificial intelligence ("AI") technologies to enhance end-of-line packaging and logistics. We have continued to strengthen our focus on Automation through strategic investments in Pickle Robot Co. ("Pickle") and a commercial partnership with Rabot Inc. ("Rabot"). Pickle is a robotics-solutions company which has developed robots for sorting, loading and unloading packaged goods. Rabot's physical AI platform uses machine vision to provide actionable insights to help businesses optimize packing workflows and minimize material waste. Together with our strategic partners, we provide customized solutions for packing environments, and believe we are uniquely positioned to respond to demand for intelligent warehouse automation.

•Geographic and Market Expansion. We believe there are significant opportunities to increase penetration across new end markets and geographies. For example, while the APAC region has a large, well-developed parcel shipping business, it currently represents less than 10% of our net revenue in 2025. We believe our Malaysia facility will continue to strengthen our performance in this region. Furthermore, growing environmental awareness and increasing regulatory trends to limit the use of polymer-based foams and plastics present an opportunity for our fiber-based protective packaging solutions. We aim to grow beyond our current PPS systems by expanding our offerings into new end-markets.

•Drive innovation. We intend to maintain and extend our technological leadership, expertise and our environmentally sustainable value proposition through continuous improvement of our product and service offerings to bolster speed, improve efficacy, and decrease packing footprint by introducing new products that deliver the environmentally friendly solutions customers require for their business needs. paragraphs: Our business faces significant risks. In addition to the summary below, you should carefully review the "Risk Factors" section of this Report. We may be subject to additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial. Our business, financial condition and results of operations could be materially adversely affected by any of these risks, and the trading prices of our common stock could decline by virtue of these risks. These risks should be read in conjunction with the other information in this Report. Some of the more significant risks relating to our business include:
•We may be unable to secure a sufficient supply of paper to meet our production requirements given the limited number of suppliers that produce paper suitable for our products.
•Adverse changes in input costs, such as kraft paper, may negatively impact us.
•Our business is exposed to risks associated with our reliance on third-party suppliers to provide both the components used in our PPS systems as well as certain fully assembled PPS systems.
•Demand for our products could be adversely affected by changes in end-user or consumer preferences.
•The loss of end-users, particularly our e-commerce end-users, or a reduction in their production requirements, could have a significant adverse impact.

paragraphs: The information in this Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations should be read together with our consolidated financial statements and related notes set forth in Part II, Item 8, as well as the discussion included in Part I, Item 1A, "Risk Factors," of this Report. This section generally discusses the results of our operations for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to the year ended December 31, 2024. For a discussion of the year ended December 31, 2024 compared to the year ended December 31, 2023, please refer to Part II, Item 7, "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024.

We are a leading provider of environmentally sustainable, systems-based, product protection and end-of-line automation solutions for e-commerce and industrial supply chains. We provide our PPS systems and paper consumables to distributors and certain select end-users. We operate manufacturing facilities in the United States, Europe and Asia. For our Automation product lines, we currently have dedicated facilities in Shelton, Connecticut and the Netherlands. R Squared Robotics, a division of Ranpak, uses three-dimensional computer vision and artificial intelligence technologies to improve end-of-line packaging and logistics functions.

We have two segments, North America and Europe/Asia. Management evaluates segment performance by net revenue and Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortization ("EBITDA") by geographic region.
We use the following key performance indicators and monitor the following other factors to analyze our business performance, determine financial forecasts, and help develop long-term strategic plans:

PPS Systems Base. We closely track the number of PPS systems installed with end-users as it is a leading indicator of underlying business trends and near-term and ongoing net revenue expectations. Our installed base of PPS systems also drives our capital expenditure budgets. The following table presents our installed base of PPS systems as of December 31, 2025 and 2024:

Paper and Other Costs. Paper is a key component of our cost of goods sold and paper costs can fluctuate significantly between periods. We purchase both 100% virgin and 100% recycled paper, as well as blends, from various suppliers for conversion into the paper consumables we sell. The cost of paper supplies is our largest input cost, and we historically have negotiated supply and pricing arrangements with most of our paper suppliers annually, with a view towards mitigating fluctuations in paper cost. Nevertheless, as paper is a commodity, its price on the open market, and in turn the prices we negotiate with suppliers at a given point in time, can fluctuate significantly, and is affected by several factors outside of our control, including inflationary pressures, supply and demand and the cost of other commodities that are used in the manufacture of paper, including wood, energy, and chemicals. For example, energy prices in Europe have experienced recent increased volatility, and such volatility has, in the past, increased the cost of paper. The market for our solutions is competitive and it may be difficult to pass on increases in paper prices to our customers immediately, or at all, which has in the past, and could in the future, adversely affect our operating results. Although we look to pass increased market costs on to our customers to mitigate the impact of these costs, we are unable to predict our ability to pass these costs on to our customers and how much of these increases we will be able to pass on to our customers. As such, we expect some continued pressure on our gross margin in the medium term relative to our historical margin profile.

Effect of Currency Fluctuations. As a result of the geographic diversity of our operations, we are exposed to the effects of currency translation, which has affected the comparability of our results of operations between the periods presented in this Report and may affect the comparability of our results of operations in future periods. Currency transaction exposure results when we generate net revenue in one currency at one time and incur expenses in another currency at another time,

or when we realize gain or loss on intercompany transfers. While we seek to limit currency transaction exposure by matching the currencies in which we incur sales and expenses, we may not always be able to do so.

In addition, we are subject to currency translation exposure because the operations of our subsidiaries are measured in their functional currency which is the currency of the primary economic environment in which the subsidiary operates. Any currency balances that are denominated in currencies other than the functional currency of the subsidiary are re-measured into the functional currency, with the resulting gain or loss recorded in the foreign currency (gains) losses line-item in our Consolidated Statements of Operations and Comprehensive Income (Loss). In turn, subsidiary income statement balances that are denominated in currencies other than USD are translated into USD, our reporting currency, in consolidation using the average exchange rate in effect during each fiscal month during the period, with any related gain or loss recorded as foreign currency translation adjustments in other comprehensive income (loss). The assets and liabilities of subsidiaries that use functional currencies other than the USD are translated into USD in consolidation using period end exchange rates, with the effects of foreign currency translation adjustments included in accumulated other comprehensive income (loss).

We hedge some of our exposure to foreign currency translation with a cross-currency swap. Refer to Note 8 — Derivative Instruments to the consolidated financial statements included elsewhere in this Report for additional information. Significant currency fluctuations could impact the comparability of results between periods, while such fluctuations coupled with material mismatches in net revenue and expenses could also adversely impact our cash flows. See "Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk."

Inflationary Pressures and Other Costs. We have continued to experience inflationary pressures in 2025, which have adversely impacted some of our end-users, such as automotive companies; distributors; electronic manufacturers; machinery manufacturers; e-commerce and mail-order fulfillment firms; and other end-users that are particularly sensitive to reductions in business and consumer spending by their respective customers, and which in turn have impacted our net revenue. Higher costs due to inflation were partially offset by price increases, which mitigated the impact on our operating results. However, our ability to predict or further offset inflationary cost increases in the future or during economic downturns or recessions may be limited or impacted by heightened competition for market share, an unwillingness by our customers to accept price increases or pressure to reduce selling prices if end-users reduce their volume of purchases. Inflationary pressures and associated changing interest rates and borrowing costs may also impact the ability of some of our end-users and suppliers to obtain funds for operations and capital expenditures, which could negatively impact our ability to obtain necessary supplies as well as the sales of materials and equipment to affected end-users. This could also result in reduced or delayed collections of outstanding accounts receivable from end-users, which could impact our cash flows. As a result, to the extent inflationary pressures continue, we expect additional pressure on our net revenue and gross margin. We will continue to evaluate the impact of inflationary pressures on our profitability and cash flows as well as our end-users.

In addition to inflationary pressures, our U.S. operations are subject to the impact of tariffs, largely related to our capital expenditures of our PPS converters, some of which are sourced from China or contain parts and components from China and other Asian countries. We are taking steps to minimize the potential impact of these tariffs by evaluating alternative parts and global suppliers as well as stepping up our efforts to refabricate and refurbish existing machines in our fleet to reduce cost. Our box customization equipment is currently made in Europe and shipped to the United States and thus will be subject to the U.S. tariff on European tariff rate. We are focused on cost reduction and efficiencies to minimize the impact to our customers, and believe in the ongoing value proposition of our equipment.

Our consolidated financial statements are prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America ("GAAP"). We also present EBITDA and AEBITDA, which are non-GAAP financial measures, because they are key measures used by our management and board of directors to understand and evaluate our operating performance and trends, to prepare and approve our annual budget and to develop short- and long-term operational plans. In particular, the exclusion of certain expenses in calculating EBITDA and AEBITDA can provide a useful measure for period-to-period comparisons of our primary business operations. We believe that EBITDA and AEBITDA provide useful information to investors and others in understanding and evaluating our operating results in the same manner as our management and board of directors.

paragraphs: Ranpak Holdings Corp. ("Ranpak," the "Company," "we," or "us") 為保護性包裝解決方案 ("PPS") 產品及電商與工業供應鏈端末自動化解決方案的領導供應商。自1972年成立以來，我們已為全球客戶提供廣泛的附加價值解決方案，同時維持對環境永續的承諾。我們所有包裝解決方案皆為100%可回收、可更新及可生物分解。我們的自動化解決方案可減少包裝時間與材料，為客戶帶來顯著的成本節省。我們持續努力回應客戶需求，並開發創新產品與全面解決方案，以提升供應鏈表現、降低成本與環境影響，並創造價值。

2025 年，本公司產生淨銷售額為 395.0 百萬美元。本公司的營業收入地理分佈多元，其中約 47% 的 2025 年淨銷售額來自北美，約 45% 來自歐洲，約 8% 來自亞洲及其他地區。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司已安裝系統數量超過 145,000 套，服務終端用戶超過 30,000 名。本公司歷來受益於具再現性且具吸引力毛利率的淨銷售額，來自已安裝系統的基礎，導致每 PPS 系統具備強勁的回本期及投資資本回報率。
我們認為，我們的業務受益於多項因素，這些因素將推動我們未來的成長：
•電商成長。電商是我們業務的重要成長動力。我們約40% 的淨銷售額來自電商終端用戶的銷售。我們持續認為，全球對電商的投資為我們帶來顯著的機會，因為電商持續成長，且成長速度超過零售銷售的成長。
•對自動化與機械視覺的需求。我們的自動化與機械視覺產品線為許多高產量企業提供顯著的端末包裝速度提升、減少勞動力、材料與運輸成本，並產生有關端末表現的寶貴數據與統計資訊。隨著企業持續關注效率與自動化解決方案，我們認為許多企業將尋求改進生產效率與品質的方法，進一步推動對我們自動化與機械視覺產品線的需求。

•拓展冷鏈市場。2025年，銷售至食品與飲料產業終端用戶的收入約佔我們淨銷售額的3%。但我們認為，企業與消費者正日益表現出對環境永續冷鏈解決方案的偏好，以在運輸途中保持食品與飲料的冷度。我們已擴展產品線，包含纖維基底內襯與永續植物基冷包，以在將易腐商品送達消費者時保持冷度，例如 RecyCold® climaliner Plus™。創新解決方案如 RecyCold Climaliner plus 代表一種100% 紙基可回收內襯替代發泡聚苯乙烯泡沫或其他較不永續的冷鏈選項，同時仍確保產品在72小時內維持在理想溫度範圍內。
•聚焦永續性。我們認為，對環境永續包裝解決方案的偏好將是未來成長的關鍵驅動因素，特別是在塑膠及其他樹脂基解決方案受到日益嚴格的公眾關注與監管壓力的情況下，我們認為消費者持續表現出對環境永續解決方案的偏好。例如，我們認為有顯著的機會透過對傳統塑膠郵件的環境友好替代方案來擴展我們的消耗性產品線，例如 naturemailer™，一種完全可回收的郵件，使用蜂巢紙絕緣材料。
•持續產品開發與創新。我們認為，我們持續創新並透過內部開發與併購 ("M&A") 將產品加入產品組合的能力，將為我們帶來額外的成長機會。
•地理擴張。歷來，地理擴張推動了我們的成長，我們認為進一步的地理擴張與現有市場的滲透將持續推動我們未來的成長。我們在馬來西亞的全功能紙張轉換設施於2024年下半年開始運作，我們認為馬來西亞設施持續改善我們服務該地區客戶的能力，同時縮短交貨時間，並為亞太（"APAC"）市場提供更具吸引力的成本結構，這是我們歷來所無法提供的。
結合當地的據點與與東南亞的連結，我們認為馬來西亞設施可以持續帶來有利的成長機會。
我們致力於強化我們作為創新永續包裝與端點自動化及機械視覺解決方案的全球領導供應商的地位。為達成這些目標，我們專注於以下戰略優先事項：

•自動化與機械視覺。我們的自動化產品在2025年佔我們淨銷售額的10%，與2024年的8%相比。我們認為自動化將成為成長的重要平台，使我們能更好地服務有更高需求量與更複雜端點需求的終端用戶。2021年，我們成立了R Squared Robotics，為Ranpak的子公司，該部門運用三維電腦視覺與人工智慧（"AI"）技術，以提升端點包裝與物流。我們持續透過戰略投資於Pickle Robot Co.（"Pickle"）與與Rabot Inc.（"Rabot"）的商業合作夥伴關係，強化對自動化的關注。Pickle是一家機器人解決方案公司，已開發用於分揀、裝載與卸載包裝商品的機器人。Rabot的實體AI平台運用機械視覺，提供行動見解，協助企業優化包裝作業流程並減少材料浪費。透過與我們的戰略夥伴合作，我們為包裝環境提供客製化解決方案，並認為我們獨具優勢，能回應對智慧倉庫自動化的需求。

•地理與市場擴張。我們認為在新終端市場與地理區域增加滲透率有著顯著的機會。例如，雖然APAC地區擁有龐大的、已發展的包裹運輸業務，但目前僅佔我們2025年淨銷售額的不到10%。我們認為馬來西亞設施將持續強化我們在該地區的表現。此外，日益增長的環境意識與增加的規範趨勢，限制使用聚合物基泡沫與塑料，為我們的纖維基保護包裝解決方案提供了機會。我們旨在超越目前的PPS系統，透過擴展至新的終端市場來擴大業務。
•推動創新。我們意圖透過持續改善產品與服務的提供，維持並拓展我們的技術領導地位、專業知識與環境永續價值主張，以提升速度、改善效果、減少包裝體積，並引入新產品，提供客戶所需符合其業務需求的環境友善解決方案。我們最近的創新包括：

paragraphs: 本 Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations 中的資訊應與我們的合併財務報表及相關附註，載於第二部分，項目 8，以及第一部分，項目 1A，"Risk Factors" 的討論一併閱讀。本節一般討論我們在 2025 年 12 月 31 日結算年度的營運結果，與 2024 年 12 月 31 日結算年度的比較。如需瞭解 2024 年 12 月 31 日結算年度與 2023 年 12 月 31 日結算年度的比較，請參閱我們 2024 年 12 月 31 日結算年度的 10-K 年度報告，第二部分，項目 7，"Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations"。

我們是 e-commerce 和工業供應鏈領域的環境永續、系統化、產品保護及端站自動化解決方案的領導供應商。我們向經銷商及部分指定終端用戶提供 PPS 系統與紙張消耗品。我們在美國、歐洲及亞洲設有製造廠。針對我們的自動化產品線，目前我們在康乃狄克州 Shelton 和荷蘭設有專用廠區。R Squared Robotics，為 Ranpak 的一個部門，使用三維電腦視覺與人工智慧技術，以改善端站包裝與物流功能。
我們有兩個應報告分部，分別為北美與歐洲/亞洲。管理階層透過各地理區域的淨營收與 Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortization（"EBITDA"）來評估分部表現。
我們使用以下關鍵績效指標，並監測其他因素以分析我們的營運表現、確定財務預測，並協助制定長期戰略計畫：
PPS 系統基礎。我們密切追蹤與終端用戶安裝的 PPS 系統數量，因為這是反映基礎營運趨勢與近期及持續淨營收預期的領先指標。我們安裝的 PPS 系統基礎也驅動我們的資本支出預算。下表顯示我們截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日及 2024 年 12 月 31 日的 PPS 系統安裝基礎：

紙張與其他成本。紙張是我們成本中的一個重要零組件，紙張成本在不同期間可能會有顯著波動。我們從多個供應商處購買 100% 原生紙與 100% 循環紙，以及混合紙，用以轉換成我們銷售的紙張消耗品。紙張供應品的成本是我們最大的投入成本，我們歷來每年與大多數紙張供應商進行供應與價格安排協議，以緩解紙張成本的波動。然而，由於紙張為一商品，其在公開市場的價格，以及我們在特定時間點與供應商協議的價格，可能會有顯著波動，且受多種我們無法控制的因素影響，包括通貨膨脹壓力、供給與需求，以及用於紙張製造的其他商品成本，包括木材、能源與化學品。例如，歐洲的能源價格近期經歷了顯著波動，過去這種波動已提高紙張成本。我們解決方案的市場競爭激烈，可能難以立即或完全將紙張價格的上漲轉嫁給客戶，這在過去已對我們的營運結果產生負面影響，未來也可能會如此。儘管我們希望將市場成本轉嫁給客戶以緩解這些成本的影響，但我們無法預測我們能否將這些成本轉嫁給客戶，以及我們能轉嫁多少這些漲幅。因此，我們預期在中長期內，我們的毛利率會相對於歷史毛利率表現持續受到壓力。
貨幣波動的影響。由於我們營運的地理多樣性，我們會受到貨幣轉換影響，這已影響本報告中所列期間的營運結果可比性，也可能影響未來期間的營運結果可比性。當我們在某一時間點以一種貨幣產生淨營收，而在另一時間點以另一種貨幣產生費用時，就會產生貨幣交易風險。
或當我們實現跨公司交易的損益時。雖然我們透過匹配銷售與費用所使用的貨幣來限制外幣交易風險，但我們可能無法總是做到這一點。

此外，我們面臨外幣折算風險，因為我們子公司之營運是以其功能貨幣計量，而功能貨幣為子公司所處主要經濟環境的貨幣。任何以非子公司功能貨幣計價的外幣餘額，會重新計價為功能貨幣，所產生的損益會記入我們合併財務報表之綜合損益（損失）中的外幣（損益）項目。換句話說，以非美元計價的子公司損益會在合併時以美元（我們的報導貨幣）進行平均交換率換算，任何相關損益會記入其他綜合損益（損失）中的外幣折算調整。使用非美元功能貨幣的子公司資產與負債會在合併時以期末交換率換算為美元，外幣折算調整的影響會計入累積其他綜合損益（損失）。
我們透過跨貨幣掉換來對衝部分外幣折算風險。請參閱本報告其他處所附的合併財務報表之附註 8 — 衍生金融工具，以取得更多資訊。顯著的貨幣波動可能影響不同期間的結果可比性，而這種波動與淨收入與費用的重大不匹配，也可能對我們的現金流產生不利影響。請參閱『市場風險的量化與質化揭露』。

通貨膨脹壓力與其他成本。我們在 2025 年持續面臨通貨膨脹壓力，這已對一些終端用戶造成負面影響，例如汽車公司；經銷商；電子製造商；機械製造商；電商與郵購履行公司；以及其他對其客戶的企業與消費者支出減少特別敏感的終端用戶，這進而影響我們的淨收入。因通貨膨脹導致的更高成本部分被價格上漲所抵銷，這減輕了對我們營運結果的影響。然而，我們預測或進一步抵銷未來或經濟衰退期間的通貨膨脹成本增加的能力可能受到限制，或受到市場份額競爭加劇、客戶不願接受價格上漲或在終端用戶減少購買量的情況下被迫降低銷售價格的影響。通貨膨脹壓力與相關的利率與借款成本變動，也可能影響一些終端用戶與供應商取得資金進行營運與資本支出的能力，這可能會對我們取得必要供應品以及向受影響的終端用戶銷售材料與設備的能力產生負面影響。這也可能導致對受影響終端用戶的應收帳款回收延遲或減少，進而影響我們的現金流。因此，若通貨膨脹壓力持續，我們預期將對我們的淨收入與毛利率產生額外壓力。我們將持續評估通貨膨脹壓力對我們利潤與現金流的影響，以及對終端用戶的影響。

除了通貨膨脹壓力，我們的美國營運也受到關稅的影響，主要與我們 PPS 轉換器的資本支出有關，其中一些設備來自中國或包含來自中國及其他亞洲國家的零組件。我們正在採取措施以減少這些關稅的潛在影響，包括評估替代零組件與全球供應商，以及加強我們現有機械隊伍的重製與翻新工作，以降低成本。我們的盒子客製化設備目前在歐洲製造並運送到美國，因此將受到美國對歐洲關稅率的影響。我們專注於成本降低與效率提升，以最小化對客戶的影響，並相信我們設備的持續價值主張。

我們的合併財務報表是根據美國通用會計準則（"GAAP"）編製。我們也提供 EBITDA 與 AEBITDA，這些是非 GAAP 財務指標，因為它們是我們管理階層與董事會用來理解與評估我們營運表現與趨勢、準備與批准年度預算，以及制定短期與長期營運計畫的關鍵指標。特別是，在計算 EBITDA 與 AEBITDA 時排除某些費用，可以提供一個有用的指標，用以比較我們主要營運活動的不同時期表現。我們認為 EBITDA 與 AEBITDA 可為投資者及其他人士提供有用的資訊，以與我們管理階層與董事會相同的方式理解與評估我們的營運結果。

headings: 與本公司業務相關的風險
由於紙張供應商數量有限，我們可能無法取得足夠的紙張以滿足生產需求。
紙漿等投入成本的不利變動，可能對我們的營運結果，包括毛利邊際，以及財務狀況產生負面影響。
由於最終用戶或消費者偏好的變動，可能對我們產品的需求產生負面影響，進而對我們的業務、財務狀況或營運結果造成重大不利影響。
最終用戶，特別是電商用戶的流失，或其生產需求減少，可能對我們的淨銷售額與獲利能力產生重大負面影響。
我們在研究與開發上的投資可能無法達到預期成果。
本公司業務的全球性特質，使我們面臨許多風險，這些風險可能對我們的財務狀況或營運結果造成重大不利影響。
本公司裝配及配送作業的重大損失或中斷可能對本公司業務、財務狀況或營運成果產生不利影響。
外幣與美元之間的波動可能對本公司合併財務狀況或營運成果產生重大影響。
本公司可能面臨營運中斷及/或勞動成本增加的風險。
本公司需面對多種不斷演進的環境及政府法規與產品登記法規，可能使本公司面臨潛在財務責任及營運成本增加的風險。
本公司面臨與氣候變遷及永續議題相關的風險，包括氣候變遷的影響。
產品責任索賠或法規行動可能對本公司財務結果產生不利影響，或損害本公司聲譽及品牌價值。
法律或法規的變更，或未能遵守任何法律及法規，可能對本公司業務、投資及營運成果產生不利影響。
本公司因業務需要，可能涉及訴訟，若未投保或保險費用上漲，可能對本公司營業成果與財務狀況造成不利影響。
與本公司證券持有相關之風險
本公司現有發行股份中，可能有相當大比例的股份在近期內出售至市場，這可能會導致本公司普通股的市場價格大幅下跌，即使本公司營運狀況良好。
本公司部分股東，包括 JS Capital，持有本公司投票權股份之相當大比例。
本公司章程中之條款可能阻礙本公司被收購，這可能會限制投資人未來願意為本公司 A 級普通股支付之價格，並可能使管理層地位更加鞏固。
這可能會限制本公司股東取得對與本公司或本公司董事、高階管理人員、股東、員工或代理人之間爭議之有利司法訴訟管轄權之能力。
紐約證券交易所可能將本公司證券從其交易場所除牌，這可能會限制投資人進行本公司證券交易之能力，並使本公司面臨更多交易限制。
本公司證券之價格已出現波動，並可能持續波動。
與我們負債相關的風險
我們的負債金額若過高，可能會不利於我們的財務狀況及履行我們義務的能力。
paragraphs: 本公司業務面臨重大風險。除下列總結外，您應仔細審閱本報告的『風險因素』部分。本公司可能面臨其他尚未為本公司所知或目前認為不重要之風險與不確定性。任何這些風險都可能對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成重大不利影響，並可能導致本公司普通股交易價格因這些風險而下跌。這些風險應與本報告中的其他資訊一併閱讀。與本公司業務相關的一些較重要風險包括：
•因紙張供應商數量有限，本公司可能無法取得足夠的紙張以滿足生產需求。
•如紙漿紙等投入成本出現不利變動，可能對本公司造成負面影響。
•本公司業務因依賴第三方供應商提供用於PPS系統的零組件以及部分組裝完成的PPS系統，而面臨相關風險。
•因終端用戶或消費者偏好變動，可能導致本公司產品需求受到不利影響。
•終端用戶，尤其是電商終端用戶流失，或其生產需求減少，可能對本公司造成重大不利影響。
